body:
## The buy

Niko Brothers, the channel that buys RVs and trucks from salvage auctions sight unseen, has a new coach: a 2020 Newmar Bay Star Sport that Ivan won at a salvage auction [1]. The video's description says he got it for a fraction of its original price; the price reveal is in the video, and it hasn't appeared in any text we could read, so the purchase price here is unknown [1]. The auction isn't named.

The Bay Star Sport is Newmar's shorter gas Class A, a motorhome built on a truck chassis rather than a diesel pusher like the Monaco the brothers took on in October. That makes it a different kind of gamble: cheaper to run and repair underneath, but with the same expensive molded bodywork at the front.

## The damage

The description lists serious front-end damage, including missing front wheels [1]. That's all we know in detail. Missing front wheels can mean a coach was stripped on the lot after a crash or that the wheels were damaged and removed; either way it can't roll until they're replaced.

The good news is in the title: the brothers drove it 600 miles home [1]. A coach that can make that trip has a running engine, a working transmission and a front end straight enough to steer.

## The work and the parts

No parts have been itemized in text, so the list in this file is our estimate of what a front-end hit with missing wheels usually needs, priced as estimates. First, two front wheels and tires, without which it couldn't move: about $1,200. Second, the front cap, the large fiberglass molding that forms the nose of a Class A, which is often the most expensive panel on the coach; a used or aftermarket cap plus paint runs about $4,000. Third, headlights and front lighting, about $800. Fourth, a check of the hubs, steering and alignment after losing the wheels, about $600. That's about $6,600 in estimated parts, before anything the video shows that we haven't seen.

We'll replace those estimates with the brothers' numbers as they give them.

## The money

In: unknown purchase price, plus an estimated $6,600 in front-end parts, plus fuel for 600 miles.

Out: clean 2020 Bay Star Sports are not cheap. A San Diego dealer lists a 3014 floorplan with 27,513 miles at $86,615, down from $104,500 [2], and a Florida dealer lists one with 8,703 miles at $120,645 against a $147,756 sticker [3]. RV Trader has more 2020 Bay Stars for sale for comparison [4].

This one will carry a branded title once repaired. A rebuilt title on an RV typically takes a large bite out of the value and can make financing and insurance harder [5]. We put the finished coach at $45,000 to $70,000, the low end assuming buyers discount heavily for front-end structural work.

## What's next

With the coach home, the work is the front end: the cap, the lights and whatever is behind them. If the damage stops at the bodywork, this could be one of the brothers' better buys. We'll add the price, the parts and the result as they post them.
